svg.title: One command
svg.desc: Animated diagram of omacvm. Left: a Mac terminal runs omacvm, which first asks a few questions (build here or download, how much of the Mac the VM gets as Low, Balanced, High or Best, the recommended settings, your user name and password), shows a summary and then works through its steps: the temporary try-omarchy live installer, the VM settings and an NVMe disk, Arch Linux ARM onto the disk, booting from it, Omarchy from omarchy-mac, virtio drivers, OmacVM on the Mac and in the VM (display, clipboard, memory, keyboard, gestures, workspaces, bridge, wallpaper), the Dock icon and Omanotch, and ends with the VM rebooting into Omarchy. Right: the VM's screen follows along, from the live installer to Arch Linux ARM to Omarchy's installer to the finished Omarchy desktop, and a checklist ticks off each stage.
svg.text: omacvm: from nothing to Omarchy, in one go

g.text: Build here or download a prebuilt VM? [build]
OmacVM.app · 12 CPUs · 32 GB · keyboard from the Mac
temporary live installer (try-omarchy, about 1.4 GB download)
VM settings and a 128 GB NVMe disk
Arch Linux ARM onto the NVMe disk (10.0.2.15)
boot from the NVMe disk, drop the live installer
system: SSH from the Mac, bootable snapshots, DNS fallback
Done. VM 'Omarchy' is rebooting into Omarchy.
